chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever restrains his hand from the people, he restrains only one hand from them, and they will restrain from him many hands.'

key_terms.أَيْدِياً كَثِيرَةً: many hands — the collective response of society; a single act of harm invites multiple acts of retaliation
key_terms.كَفَّ يَدَهُ: restrained his hand — a phrase meaning to refrain from harming, interfering with, or aggressing against others

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about restraining one's hand from harming people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) teaches a principle of social reciprocity: a person who harms or aggresses against others may withdraw one hand of harm, but they invite many retaliating hands against themselves. This hadith counsels against harming others by illustrating the natural social consequence — those who refrain from harming people protect themselves from far greater collective retaliation. The teaching reflects the wisdom of peaceful coexistence in a tribal society where collective retaliation was a well-understood social norm.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Huzeyfa Bin Mansour who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who restrains his hand from the people, so rather he has restrained one hand from them, and they would be restraining from him, a lot of hands’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who has said the following: “
I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Whoever holds his hands off the people has held back only one hand, however, they will hold many hands off of him.’”
